findings.body:
In src/lib.rs line 4, `xs.iter().position(...)` is wrapped in `unwrap_or(0)` and then `Some(...)`, so a missing element yields `Some(0)` instead of `None`. The caller `contains` in src/use_it.rs line 4 is `position(xs, x).is_some()`, so it now returns true for every absent value, including on an empty slice.

Trigger: Any call to position or contains where x is not in xs, including an empty slice.”

Impact: `position` returns `Some(0)` for any value not in the slice, and `use_it::contains` reports true for absent values. Any consumer relying on `None` for not-found gets false positives.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `Some(...unwrap_or(0))` wrapper and return `xs.iter().position(|v| *v == x)` as before.
findings.title: position returns Some(0) for absent elements, so contains reports false matches

findings.body:
position() now returns Some(0) when x is absent, because unwrap_or(0) replaces the None case. The caller contains() in use_it.rs tests position(xs, x).is_some(), so it now returns true for every input, including values missing from xs.

Trigger: Calling contains(xs, x) or position(xs, x) with an x that is not present in xs.

Impact: util::contains (public via use_it) reports true for absent values, so any caller relying on it for membership checks gets wrong answers. position() callers that expect None for not-found also break.
findings.suggestion: Revert to returning xs.iter().position(|v| *v == x) so None still means not found, or update the callers and the signature together.
findings.title: position() returns Some(0) for missing values, so contains() is always true

risk_level.reason: The change silently alters the public position function so a missing element returns Some(0) instead of None, a semantic break that callers relying on None will misread as a found match at index 0.
